paragraphs: My name is Lily, and I am ten years old. Pat is eight, and his birthday was on Sunday. He loves a picture book about a bear on skis. So I made a card with a bear on it. Do you want to make one too? First, get the things that you need. You need white paper and an empty cereal box. You also need scissors, glue, and a fat black pen. I keep a dictionary on my desk for the spelling.

Step one: Cut the empty box into a square. Step two: Fold the white paper in half. Step three: Glue the square on the front. Step four: Draw a bear on the square with the fat pen. Draw two long skis under the feet of the bear. Tom looked at my card and smiled. "The bear needs ears," he said. "Good idea," I said.

Step five: Cut a small circle from the box. Step six: Glue the circle on the head of the bear. Now the bear has one ear. Repeat steps five and six for the second ear. Be careful with the scissors. Ask an adult to help if you need it. Do not cut too fast, and keep your fingers away from the blade. Now the bear has two ears.

Last, write inside the card. I wanted to write the word "adventure." I was not sure about the spelling. I looked in the dictionary and found it. Then I wrote, "Happy birthday, Pat! Have a good adventure!" Pat opened the card on Sunday. "A bear on skis!" he said. He put the card on his shelf.
